example.title: SQL Query on Orders Data
example.code:
-- Find top customers by total spending
-- Using the e-commerce orders table

SELECT 
    u.user_id,
    u.name,
    COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders,
    SUM(o.amount_usd) AS total_spent,
    AVG(o.amount_usd) AS avg_order_value,
    MAX(o.order_date) AS last_order
FROM orders o
JOIN users u ON o.user_id = u.user_id
WHERE o.order_date >= '2024-01-01'
GROUP BY u.user_id, u.name
HAVING SUM(o.amount_usd) > 100
ORDER BY total_spent DESC
LIMIT 10;

-- Result:

example.title: Python — Clean Raw Order Data
example.code:
import json
from datetime import datetime

def clean_order(raw: dict) -> dict:
    """Clean a raw e-commerce order event."""
    
    # Parse amount: "$129.99" → 129.99
    amount_str = raw.get("amount", "$0")
    amount = float(amount_str.replace("$", "").replace(",", ""))
    
    # Parse timestamp
    ts = datetime.fromisoformat(
        raw["timestamp"].replace("Z", "+00:00")
    )
    
    # Normalize device type
    device = raw.get("device", "unknown").lower()
    if "iphone" in device or "android" in device:
        device_type = "mobile"
    elif "ipad" in device or "tablet" in device:
        device_type = "tablet"
    else:
        device_type = "desktop"
    
    return {
        "order_id": raw["order_id"],
        "user_id": raw["user_id"],
        "product_id": raw.get("product_id"),  # handle null
        "amount_usd": amount,
        "order_date": ts.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"),
        "device_type": device_type,
        "city": raw.get("shipping_address", {}).get("city"),
    }

# Usage:
raw_order = json.loads(api_response)
clean = clean_order(raw_order)
print(clean)
# {'order_id': 'ord_20240115_9182', 'user_id': 'usr_9182', 
#  'amount_usd': 129.99, 'device_type': 'mobile', ...}

lesson.overview: Data modeling is the process of designing how data is structured, stored, and accessed. It starts with conceptual models (what entities exist), then logical models (how they relate), then physical models (how they're stored). Good data models make analytics fast, reliable, and cost-effective.

example.title: Conceptual Model → Star Schema — E-Commerce
example.code:
═══════════════════════════════════════════════
 CONCEPTUAL DATA MODEL — E-Commerce Platform
═══════════════════════════════════════════════

 Business Entities (What exists in our domain?)
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────

 📦 CUSTOMER         🛒 ORDER           📋 PRODUCT
 ├─ Name             ├─ Order Date       ├─ Product Name
 ├─ Email            ├─ Total Amount     ├─ Category
 ├─ City             ├─ Payment Method   ├─ Price
 └─ Segment          └─ Shipping Status  └─ Brand

 📅 TIME             🏪 STORE
 ├─ Date             ├─ Store Name
 ├─ Month            ├─ Region
 ├─ Quarter          └─ Store Type
 └─ Year


 Relationships (How do they connect?)
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────

 CUSTOMER ──┐
            ├──< ORDER >──┬── PRODUCT
 TIME ──────┘             │
                          └── STORE

 • A Customer places many Orders        (1:M)
 • An Order contains many Products       (M:M → bridge table)
 • An Order happens at one Time          (M:1)
 • An Order is placed at one Store       (M:1)


 Business Questions This Model Answers:
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────

 ✅ "What is total revenue by product category per quarter?"
 ✅ "Who are our top 10 customers by lifetime value?"
 ✅ "Which stores have the highest average order value?"
 ✅ "What is the month-over-month revenue growth?"
 ✅ "Which customer segment buys the most premium products?"


═══════════════════════════════════════════════
 FROM CONCEPTUAL → PHYSICAL (Star Schema)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════

 The conceptual model above translates into:

 ⭐ fact_orders (grain: one row per order line item)
    ├─ order_key (PK)
    ├─ customer_key (FK → dim_customers)
    ├─ product_key  (FK → dim_products)
    ├─ date_key     (FK → dim_date)
    ├─ store_key    (FK → dim_stores)
    ├─ amount_usd   (measure)
    ├─ quantity      (measure)
    └─ discount_pct  (measure)

 💎 dim_customers         💎 dim_products
    ├─ customer_key (PK)     ├─ product_key (PK)
    ├─ name                  ├─ product_name
    ├─ email                 ├─ category
    ├─ city                  ├─ brand
    └─ segment               └─ price

 💎 dim_date              💎 dim_stores
    ├─ date_key (PK)         ├─ store_key (PK)
    ├─ full_date             ├─ store_name
    ├─ month                 ├─ region
    ├─ quarter               └─ store_type
    └─ year

lesson.overview: Dimensional modeling is a data warehouse design technique that structures data into fact tables (measurable events) and dimension tables (descriptive context). The star schema is the most common pattern.

example.title: Create Star Schema Tables
example.code:
-- FACT TABLE: Each row = one order event
CREATE TABLE fact_orders (
    order_key       BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
    user_key        BIGINT REFERENCES dim_users(user_key),
    product_key     BIGINT REFERENCES dim_products(product_key),
    date_key        INT    REFERENCES dim_date(date_key),
    amount_usd      DECIMAL(10,2),
    quantity        INT,
    discount_pct    DECIMAL(5,2),
    shipping_cost   DECIMAL(10,2)
);

-- DIMENSION: Users
CREATE TABLE dim_users (
    user_key    BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id     VARCHAR(50),
    name        VARCHAR(100),
    email       VARCHAR(100),
    city        VARCHAR(50),
    state       VARCHAR(2),
    segment     VARCHAR(20),  -- 'premium', 'standard'
    valid_from  DATE,
    valid_to    DATE,          -- SCD Type 2
    is_current  BOOLEAN
);

-- DIMENSION: Products  
CREATE TABLE dim_products (
    product_key   BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
    product_id    VARCHAR(50),
    name          VARCHAR(200),
    category      VARCHAR(50),
    brand         VARCHAR(50),
    price_tier    VARCHAR(20)   -- 'budget', 'mid', 'premium'
);

example.title: PySpark — Aggregate Orders at Scale
example.code:
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("OrdersAggregation") \
    .getOrCreate()

# Read orders from Delta Lake
orders = spark.read.format("delta").load("s3://data-lake/orders/")

# Daily revenue by product category
daily_revenue = (
    orders
    .join(products, "product_id")
    .groupBy(
        F.col("order_date"),
        F.col("category")
    )
    .agg(
        F.sum("amount_usd").alias("revenue"),
        F.count("order_id").alias("order_count"),
        F.avg("amount_usd").alias("avg_order_value"),
        F.countDistinct("user_id").alias("unique_customers")
    )
    .orderBy("order_date", "category")
)

# Add 7-day rolling average
window_7d = Window \
    .partitionBy("category") \
    .orderBy("order_date") \
    .rowsBetween(-6, 0)

result = daily_revenue.withColumn(
    "rolling_7d_avg",
    F.avg("revenue").over(window_7d)
)

# Write back to Delta Lake
result.write \
    .format("delta") \
    .mode("overwrite") \
    .save("s3://data-lake/analytics/daily_revenue/")

# Cmd 1 — Read raw orders from S3
raw_orders = spark.read \
    .format("json") \
    .load("s3://raw-data/orders/2024/01/")

display(raw_orders.limit(5))
# +------------------+---------+--------+-------------------------+
# | order_id         | user_id | amount | timestamp               |
# +------------------+---------+--------+-------------------------+
# | ord_20240115_9182| usr_9182| $129.99| 2024-01-15T14:32:11.294Z|
# | ord_20240115_4471| usr_4471| $49.00 | 2024-01-15T15:01:22.100Z|
# +------------------+---------+--------+-------------------------+

# Cmd 2 — Clean and transform
from pyspark.sql.functions import *

clean_orders = raw_orders \
    .withColumn("amount_usd", 
        regexp_replace(col("amount"), "[$,]", "").cast("double")) \
    .withColumn("order_date", 
        to_date(col("timestamp"))) \
    .withColumn("device_type",
        when(col("device").contains("iPhone"), "mobile")
        .when(col("device").contains("iPad"), "tablet")
        .otherwise("desktop")) \
    .drop("amount", "timestamp", "device")

# Cmd 3 — Write to Delta Lake
clean_orders.write \
    .format("delta") \
    .mode("append") \
    .partitionBy("order_date") \
    .saveAsTable("prod.ecommerce.orders")

print(f"✅ Loaded {clean_orders.count()} orders")

example.title: AI Feature Pipeline — Order Predictions
example.code:
# Build features for ML from orders data
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

def build_user_features(orders_df):
    """Generate ML features from order history."""
    
    w30 = Window.partitionBy("user_id") \
        .orderBy("order_date") \
        .rangeBetween(-30, 0)
    
    features = orders_df.groupBy("user_id").agg(
        # Recency
        F.datediff(F.current_date(), F.max("order_date"))
            .alias("days_since_last_order"),
        # Frequency
        F.count("order_id").alias("total_orders"),
        F.countDistinct(F.month("order_date"))
            .alias("active_months"),
        # Monetary
        F.sum("amount_usd").alias("lifetime_value"),
        F.avg("amount_usd").alias("avg_order_value"),
        F.stddev("amount_usd").alias("order_value_std"),
        # Behavioral
        F.countDistinct("product_id")
            .alias("unique_products"),
        F.countDistinct("category")
            .alias("unique_categories"),
    )
    
    return features

# Write features to Feature Store
user_features = build_user_features(orders)
user_features.write \
    .format("delta") \
    .mode("overwrite") \
    .saveAsTable("ml.features.user_rfm")

example.code:
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════
-- 1. MATERIALIZED VIEW — Executive Dashboard
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW mv_daily_dashboard AS
SELECT 
    order_date,
    COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS daily_active_buyers,
    COUNT(order_id) AS total_orders,
    SUM(amount_usd) AS daily_revenue,
    AVG(amount_usd) AS avg_order_value,
    
    -- Year-over-year comparison
    LAG(SUM(amount_usd), 365) OVER (ORDER BY order_date) 
        AS revenue_1y_ago,
    
    -- Device breakdown
    SUM(CASE WHEN device_type = 'mobile' THEN 1 END) AS mobile_orders,
    SUM(CASE WHEN device_type = 'desktop' THEN 1 END) AS desktop_orders,
    
    -- Top category
    MODE() WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY category) AS top_category
    
FROM fact_orders f
JOIN dim_products p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
JOIN dim_date d ON f.date_key = d.date_key
GROUP BY order_date
ORDER BY order_date DESC;

example.title: PII Masking — Protect Customer Data
example.code:
import hashlib
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

def mask_pii(orders_df):
    """Mask personally identifiable information 
    before loading to analytics warehouse."""
    
    return orders_df \
        .withColumn(
            "email_hash",
            F.sha2(F.col("email"), 256)
        ) \
        .withColumn(
            "masked_name",
            F.concat(
                F.substring("name", 1, 1),
                F.lit("***")
            )
        ) \
        .withColumn(
            "masked_city",
            F.when(
                F.col("city").isNotNull(),
                F.concat(F.substring("city", 1, 3), F.lit("***"))
            )
        ) \
        .drop("email", "name", "phone", 
              "shipping_address")

# Before: {email: "sarah@example.com", name: "Sarah Chen"}
# After:  {email_hash: "a3f2...", masked_name: "S***"}

example.title: Query Optimization — Orders Table
example.code:
-- ❌ BAD: Full table scan ($$$)
SELECT * FROM orders 
WHERE order_date = '2024-01-15';
-- Scans: 500GB | Cost: $2.50 | Time: 45s

-- ✅ GOOD: Partitioned table
-- Table partitioned by order_date, clustered by user_id
SELECT user_id, amount_usd, device_type
FROM orders 
WHERE order_date = '2024-01-15'
  AND amount_usd > 50;
-- Scans: 1.2GB | Cost: $0.006 | Time: 2s
-- 💰 Savings: 99.8%

-- ✅ BETTER: Use materialized view for repeated queries
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW mv_daily_orders
PARTITION BY (order_date)
CLUSTER BY (user_id)
AS SELECT 
    order_date, user_id, 
    SUM(amount_usd) as daily_total,
    COUNT(*) as order_count
FROM orders 
GROUP BY order_date, user_id;
-- Now dashboards query the MV: 0.1GB, <1s

example.title: Interview Question — Orders Analysis
example.code:
-- INTERVIEW QUESTION: 
-- "Find users whose spending increased month-over-month
--  for 3+ consecutive months."

WITH monthly_spend AS (
    SELECT 
        user_id,
        DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS month,
        SUM(amount_usd) AS total
    FROM orders
    GROUP BY user_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date)
),
with_prev AS (
    SELECT *,
        LAG(total) OVER (
            PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY month
        ) AS prev_total,
        CASE WHEN total > LAG(total) OVER (
            PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY month
        ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS increased
    FROM monthly_spend
),
streaks AS (
    SELECT *,
        SUM(CASE WHEN increased = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) 
            OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY month) 
            AS streak_group
    FROM with_prev
)
SELECT DISTINCT user_id
FROM streaks
GROUP BY user_id, streak_group
HAVING SUM(increased) >= 3;

example.title: Decision Framework
example.code:
✅ Data Engineering is for you if:
  • You like building systems, not just analyzing data
  • You enjoy automation and scripting
  • You're comfortable with code (or want to be)
  • You want high salary potential ($120k–$700k+)
  • You like solving infrastructure problems

❌ Consider other roles if:
  • You prefer making charts and presentations → Data Analyst
  • You want to build ML models → Data Scientist
  • You want to build user-facing apps → Software Engineer

📊 Your first test: Try the SQL demo in Phase 1.
   If you enjoy it, you're on the right track!

example.title: Data Catalog Entry — Orders Table
example.code:
# Unity Catalog / OpenMetadata definition
table:
  name: fact_orders
  database: prod.ecommerce
  owner: data-engineering-team
  
  classification: CONFIDENTIAL
  pii_columns:
    - user_id      # pseudonymized
    - shipping_city # masked after 3 chars
  
  data_quality:
    freshness: 
      max_delay: 2h
      alert: pagerduty
    completeness:
      required_columns: [order_id, user_id, amount_usd]
      null_threshold: 0.01  # max 1% nulls
    uniqueness:
      primary_key: order_id
      
  lineage:
    sources:
      - raw.orders_api     # Kafka topic
      - raw.product_catalog # PostgreSQL CDC
    downstream:
      - analytics.mv_daily_dashboard
      - ml.features.user_rfm
      
  retention:
    raw_data: 90_days
    aggregated: 7_years
    pii: 30_days_after_deletion_request

example.title: Architecture Decision Record (ADR)
example.code:
ADR-007: Migrate Orders Pipeline to Delta Lake
══════════════════════════════════════════════════

Status: ACCEPTED
Date: 2024-06-15
Author: You (Staff Data Engineer)
Reviewers: VP Engineering, Data Platform Team

Context:
  Current Parquet-based orders pipeline has:
  - No ACID transactions → data corruption on failures
  - No schema evolution → breaking changes need downtime
  - No time travel → can't debug data issues

Decision:
  Migrate to Delta Lake on Databricks with:
  ✅ ACID transactions for reliable writes
  ✅ Schema evolution for backward compatibility
  ✅ Time travel for auditing & debugging
  ✅ Z-ordering on user_id for 10x faster queries

Impact:
  - Migration: 2 sprints (4 weeks)
  - Cost: +$2K/mo compute, -$8K/mo from query savings
  - Net savings: $6K/month = $72K/year
  - Risk: Low (Delta Lake is backward compatible)

This is the kind of document that gets you promoted. ↑
